articles.title: The Stakes Are High in Brazil’s Upcoming Election
articles.author: Alex MacArthur
articles.content_excerpt: For a time this summer, Brazil’s presidential election seemed Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s to lose, and Latin America’s largest democracy appeared poised to hold its ground while right-wing candidates triumphed in Colombia, Peru, Honduras, Chile, and Panama, and the Left lost its long hold on Bolivia. Before, the race had been steadily tightening between the eighty-year-old president and his forty-five-year-old challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro, the blandly affable, lacquered version of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a twenty-seven-year sentence for plotting a coup after his defeat. articles.title: West Point’s Honor Code Taught the Military to Lie
articles.author: Jasper Craven
articles.content_excerpt: On May 12, 1962, General Douglas MacArthur strode into the West Point mess hall and delivered a stirring farewell address before an audience of more than two thousand cadets. It had been just over a year since another famed former general, President Dwight D. Eisenhower, had famously delivered his own closing warning about industry’s capture of the Pentagon. Now MacArthur seemed worried about the corruption of the American soldier’s soul — the death of honor itself. Honor was everything to MacArthur. articles.title: Against the Politics of Communal Fear
articles.author: Bhaskar Sunkara
articles.content_excerpt: New York City’s new municipal strategy to combat antisemitism comes just days after the war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu used his platform at the United Nations to call Zohran Mamdani “the antisemitic mayor of New York” and claim that since his election “many Jews no longer feel safe” in the city. The initiative seeks to expand education, support victims of hate crimes, and fund security at Jewish institutions and other houses of worship throughout the five boroughs. Laudable as any attempt to reduce animus is, the Left should view the plan skeptically. Antisemitism, it goes without saying, is an evil. articles.title: A Decade After His First Presidential Run, Bernie Isn’t Alone
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: If you’re anyone who veers remotely to the left politically, there are two eras: a time before Bernie Sanders ran for president, and a time after. The US political landscape before Sanders’s first presidential campaign looks today like an alien planet. There were virtually no socialists who held elected office, or at least those who admitted to it. The Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) was an obscure organization with a little over six thousand members across twenty-six chapters. Arguably the most prominent leftist figure was a curmudgeonly linguist who almost never appeared in mainstream media, Noam Chomsky. articles.author: Marlon Ettinger
articles.content_excerpt: As a young member of the Front National (today’s Rassemblement National), Jordan Bardella was an “obsessive antisemite,” according to a story published by investigative site Mediapart this Monday. “Banks are all controlled by Jews,” Bardella allegedly wrote in one message published by Mediapart . “The Jew must dominate other peoples, crush them and rob them,” read another. “A Zionist is necessarily Jewish, and deeply so.” Bardella, who was the Rassemblement National’s candidate for prime minister in 2024 and who has been president of the party since 2022, denies having written the messages, which Mediapart says date from between 2013 and 2015. “These comments are completely outrageous. articles.title: Drop the Charges Against Misael | No Political Arrests
articles.author: Portland DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Portland DSA resolutely denounces the political coercion by Texas State police of DSA member and Austin City Council candidate Misael Ramos, who was wrongfully arrested the morning of September 26. Ramos had recently attended a protest decrying ICE brutality, particularly the violence against Venezuelan immigrant Wilber Rafael Garces Perez who still remains critically injured after being shot by immigration police. Misael is one of many people in Texas being targeted for exercising their free speech in rightfully condemning state violence against the immigrant community. What we’re seeing is a racheting up of state repression, now targeting citizens and socialist political candidates. We will stand by our people, immigrants and poor alike, against this violence.
